The test image shows a **tomato stem cut lengthwise** near the soil line, with clear brown internal discoloration of the pith/vascular tissue. The plant has wilted (dead leaves visible on black plastic mulch). No white mycelium or sclerotia visible.

Top candidates based on stem internal discoloration:
- Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (pith discoloration)
- Verticillium_Wilt (vascular discoloration when cut)
- Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers (stem cankers near soil line)
- Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (stem brown lesions)

Now viewing one reference per class:
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt stem reference shows extensive brown pith discoloration throughout the stem when cut longitudinally — very similar to the test image. Now checking another class:
Alternaria shows external dark/black canker near soil line — quite different from the test image's internal pith discoloration. Checking Bacterial_Canker stem:
Bacterial_Canker also shows brown interior when stem is cut — a close alternative. Let me check a 4th class to complete the required coverage:

**Analysis Summary:**

- **Test image**: Tomato stem cut longitudinally near soil line. Extensive brown/tan discoloration throughout the pith/interior tissue. Green outer stem intact. Dead wilted leaves on black plastic mulch in background.

- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (Bugwood_13)**: Near-identical — stem split lengthwise showing complete brown pith discoloration throughout. Best match visually and symptomatically ("interior stem shows dark or light brown discoloration in the pith area").

- **Alternaria stem cankers (Bugwood_4)**: External dark/black canker near soil line, no internal pith view. Does not match.

- **Bacterial_Canker (Bugwood_9)**: Internal brown discoloration visible but more localized/patchy. Less uniform than test image.

- **Phytophthora_Blight (Bugwood_21)**: Dark external stem collapse — completely different appearance.

The test image's uniform extensive brown pith discoloration from a longitudinal cut, combined with collapsed wilted plant on black plastic mulch (typical commercial tomato field), most strongly matches Southern_Bacterial_Wilt caused by *Ralstonia solanacearum*.
